title: Project workbench keeps Plane-style multi-layout parity
intent: Expand Fulcrum project work so one project workbench can switch between board, list, spreadsheet, calendar, and Gantt/timeline without changing the underlying task set, filters, or saved-view identity.
acceptance: Project board URL exposes layout switcher with board, list, table, calendar, timeline choices.
Switching layouts preserves active project, selected saved view, filters, grouping, sort, and selected task ids.
All layouts call the same work-management aggregate instead of each route issuing separate CRUD queries.
Calendar and timeline are disabled only when required date/dependency data is absent and explain the missing fields.
anti_patterns: Separate unrelated routes with divergent filters for each layout.
Calendar-only task copies or timeline-only dependency copies.
Web component stitching direct database data instead of service aggregate.
interactions: Open project board, change layout to table, add a filter, switch to calendar, verify filter persists.
Select three tasks in list, switch to board, run bulk status move.
Use keyboard shortcut to cycle layouts and verify focus remains inside the workbench.
critique_focus: Does the UX feel like Plane's issue workspace while preserving Fulcrum's task/run/doc graph instead of becoming a generic kanban clone?
manual_simulation: As a project lead, review blocked tasks in board view, switch to spreadsheet for bulk triage, then calendar for due-date risk without rebuilding the query.
incentive: Turns Fulcrum work management into a durable command center instead of disconnected task views.

title: Saved views span project and workspace work scopes
intent: Add Plane-inspired saved views that persist layout, filters, display properties, grouping, sort, access, and scope for project-level and workspace-level work queues.
acceptance: SavedView stores scope as project or workspace and validates access level.
Saved view can open in board, list, table, calendar, or timeline with one shared filter model.
Workspace views can include tasks from multiple projects while still showing project badges and repo context.
Saved views have create, rename, duplicate, delete, and default-view actions.
anti_patterns: Stub CRUD router with no domain validation.
Saved filters tied only to board route query params.
Private view visibility enforced only in the client.
interactions: Create workspace view for blocked P0 tasks across projects.
Duplicate a project view, change layout from table to board, save as private.
Open saved view from command palette and verify project/repo context remains visible.
critique_focus: Are saved views powerful enough for Plane parity and still explicit about Fulcrum project/repo/run relationships?
manual_simulation: As an engineering manager, save a cross-project 'agent blocked' view and revisit it after switching projects.
incentive: Saved views become the reusable lens for every planning, review, and dispatch workflow.

title: Single filter builder powers every work layout
intent: Replace ad hoc filters with one Plane-style filter builder for status/state group, assignee, label, cycle, module, type, priority, date, dependency, run state, doc link, and search filters.
acceptance: Filter builder renders the same model in board, list, spreadsheet, calendar, timeline, reports, CLI, and TUI.
Applied filters are visible as removable chips with counts where known.
Filter query serializes to URL and SavedView without lossy field conversion.
Unsupported filters on a surface are marked unavailable rather than silently dropped.
anti_patterns: Each layout implements its own filter semantics.
Stringly typed filters that cannot validate field names or operators.
Search box pretending to be full filter builder.
interactions: Add assignee plus no-due-date plus blocked-by filter and save it.
Remove one applied chip and confirm task counts update without losing sort.
Open same saved filter in CLI/TUI and compare result count.
critique_focus: Does the filter model map Plane work-item power filters to Fulcrum-specific run/doc/context fields cleanly?
manual_simulation: Find all tasks assigned to me that have failed agent runs and no linked doc, then save that view.
incentive: Prevents every new work surface from forking query behavior.

title: Task detail becomes a relationship-rich side panel
intent: Upgrade Fulcrum task detail from edit sheet to Plane-like side panel with dense properties, rich description, activity, comments, dependencies, subitems, links, attachments/artifacts, docs, runs, memory, and audit sections.
acceptance: Opening a task preserves board/list context and browser back/forward behavior.
Panel loads one aggregate endpoint with task, project, repo, docs, dependencies, runs, artifacts, memory, comments, activity, watchers, and audit.
Properties can be edited inline with optimistic update and rollback.
Relationship rail sections are collapsible and show counts and empty states.
anti_patterns: Full-page detail replacing the current workbench by default.
Panel only editing title/status/priority/description.
Web performing N unrelated fetches from component code.
interactions: Click a board card, edit due date and assignee, expand runs, then close panel and keep board scroll position.
Open linked doc from task detail and return to same panel.
Dispatch an agent run from detail after previewing context.
critique_focus: Does detail answer 'what context and execution history does this work item have?' without burying task editing?
manual_simulation: Investigate a blocked task, read its dependency chain, recent failed run, artifact, and linked design doc from one panel.
incentive: Task detail becomes the anchor for human-agent work instead of a narrow task form.

title: Peek overview supports fast work-item preview
intent: Add Plane-style peek overview so users can inspect a task from lists, calendars, modules, cycles, and command results without fully opening the detail panel.
acceptance: Hover or keyboard preview opens a lightweight task peek with title, state, priority, assignee, due date, dependencies, run state, and linked docs count.
Peek can promote to full detail while preserving selected item and route context.
Peek respects permissions and never exposes hidden project data.
Peek works from command palette, saved views, calendar chips, and dependency trees.
anti_patterns: Tooltip with only title text.
Preview that triggers expensive full aggregate load for every hover.
Preview inaccessible by keyboard.
interactions: Keyboard through table rows and press preview shortcut.
Hover calendar chip, inspect blockers, then open full task detail.
Search in command palette, preview result, then jump to task.
critique_focus: Does preview reduce navigation churn for power users without adding fragile hover-only behavior?
manual_simulation: Triage 20 tasks in table view, peeking into each blocker chain before selecting the few needing full edits.
incentive: Speeds review-heavy workflows and makes dense Plane-style surfaces usable.

title: Cycles mirror Plane active, upcoming, completed planning
intent: Expand sprints into Plane-like cycles with active/upcoming/completed groupings, cycle detail, cycle analytics sidebar, capacity, rollover, and task assignment workflows.
acceptance: Cycles list groups active, upcoming, and completed cycles with per-cycle counts and date progress.
Cycle detail reuses workbench layouts filtered to cycle scope.
Closing a cycle prompts rollover, backlog move, or keep-in-closed-cycle for incomplete tasks.
Cycle analytics sidebar shows progress by state, assignee, label, and points/capacity where configured.
anti_patterns: Sprint list as flat CRUD table only.
Closing sprint by status toggle without incomplete-task disposition.
Separate cycle tasks that diverge from project tasks.
interactions: Create next cycle, drag backlog tasks into it, start it, close it with rollover.
Open active cycle from project dashboard and inspect progress sidebar.
Switch cycle detail from board to calendar to verify date alignment.
critique_focus: Does Fulcrum keep agile planning parity while connecting cycles to agent run throughput and project health?
manual_simulation: Plan a one-week cycle, notice over-capacity, move lower priority items back to backlog, and later close with carry-over notes.
incentive: Cycles become a planning unit, not a thin sprint label.

title: Modules group work by deliverable with progress analytics
intent: Introduce Plane-inspired modules as project deliverable containers with owner, status, target date, tasks, docs, artifacts, and progress analytics, mapped to Fulcrum's task graph rather than generic tags.
acceptance: Project overview links to modules with counts and health summary.
Module detail shows same workbench layouts scoped to module tasks.
Module can link docs, artifacts, repo paths, and runs that serve the deliverable.
Module status and target date roll up from task state and explicit module fields.
anti_patterns: Modules implemented as labels only.
Module pages that duplicate task board code.
No module-level progress or relationship rail.
interactions: Create module, add existing tasks, link design doc, dispatch run for top task, inspect module progress.
Filter project board by module and save as view.
Move task between modules and verify activity/audit entry.
critique_focus: Does module concept add delivery structure beyond labels while staying service-owned and extractable?
manual_simulation: Track a 'Docs import' deliverable through tasks, implementation runs, artifacts, and final validation notes.
incentive: Gives Fulcrum a mid-level planning object comparable to Plane modules and GitHub milestones.

title: Inbox intake triages external and agent-discovered work
intent: Add Plane-style intake/inbox for proposed work from humans, imports, repo scans, docs, failed runs, and automation before conversion into project tasks.
acceptance: Intake items support accept, decline, mark duplicate, assign project/module/cycle, and convert to task.
Intake captures source type: manual, import, doc, repo scan, run follow-up, memory candidate, automation.
Accepted items preserve source refs and create audit/activity events.
Inbox filters include status, source, priority, labels, assignee, date, and duplicate state.
anti_patterns: Every idea immediately becomes a task.
Inbox disconnected from project dashboard and command palette.
Decline action losing source evidence.
interactions: Convert failed run follow-up into task with linked artifact and source trace.
Decline duplicate intake item after linking it to original task.
Filter intake to untriaged repo-scan findings and bulk assign owner.
critique_focus: Does intake cover Fulcrum-specific sources instead of copying Plane issue intake literally?
manual_simulation: Process a morning queue of run follow-ups, imported GitHub issues, and doc TODOs into accepted tasks or declined duplicates.
incentive: Creates controlled work entry instead of polluting boards with unvetted items.

title: Power-K command system becomes context-aware work control
intent: Replace basic navigation palette with Plane-style Power-K registry supporting global, project, cycle, module, task, and selection-aware commands across work management.
acceptance: Command registry declares commands with id, title, group, shortcut, visibility predicate, execution payload, and permission requirement.
Palette shows context indicator and filters commands based on current project/task/selection/layout.
Task commands include change state, priority, assignee, cycle, module, labels, link doc, start run, preview context, and archive/delete where permitted.
Bulk commands appear only when selection exists and show selected count.
anti_patterns: Static array of links plus fuzzy search only.
Commands hiding permission failures until after execution.
Context-free commands requiring users to re-select current project/task.
interactions: Press Cmd+K on a task detail and change priority via command.
Select multiple cards and invoke bulk move to cycle.
Open palette from project dashboard and start agent run with current project prefilled.
critique_focus: Does the palette become an execution surface, not just navigation?
manual_simulation: Without touching the mouse, triage a selected task: assign owner, set due date, link doc, preview context, start agent run.
incentive: Keyboard-first control is table stakes for Plane/Linear parity and critical for agent supervision.

title: Global shortcuts respect typing and support key sequences
intent: Add Plane-style keyboard shortcut handling with modifier shortcuts, key sequences, command palette open, layout navigation, item movement, and input-safe guards.
acceptance: Shortcut engine ignores text inputs, textareas, contenteditable, and rich editors unless command explicitly allows typing context.
Shortcut overlay lists global, project, workbench, detail, and selection shortcuts.
Key sequences support workbench actions such as go to board/list/table/calendar, create task, open filters, open saved views, and focus next item.
Keyboard moves announce changes for accessibility and persist through services.
anti_patterns: Raw window keydown handlers scattered across components.
Shortcuts firing while editing task descriptions.
Overlay documenting shortcuts that are not executable.
interactions: Open shortcut overlay, trigger sequence to switch to calendar, then return to board.
Edit description and verify single-letter shortcuts do not fire.
Move card with keyboard and hear/read live announcement.
critique_focus: Can keyboard power use scale without colliding with rich text editing and command palette?
manual_simulation: Plan a sprint using only keyboard: create tasks, move status, assign cycle, open detail, and close overlay.
incentive: Makes dense work surfaces efficient and accessible.

title: Calendar view handles due-date planning and quick creation
intent: Bring Plane calendar behavior into Fulcrum with date buckets, overflow handling, unscheduled tray, sprint/cycle bands, drag reschedule, and quick create on date.
acceptance: Calendar displays tasks by due date and optionally start date without creating separate calendar entities.
Unscheduled tasks are available in a tray and can be dragged onto dates.
Date cells show limited chips with overflow expansion and keyboard access.
Quick-create on a date pre-fills project, due date, active saved-view context, and optional cycle.
anti_patterns: Static month grid with no drag or quick create.
Tasks disappearing when due date is cleared.
Calendar storing separate shadow copies.
interactions: Drag unscheduled task to Wednesday and verify due date persists.
Quick-create task on cycle end date from calendar cell.
Expand a crowded day and open task peek.
critique_focus: Does calendar fit planning workflows, not just display dates?
manual_simulation: Review next two weeks, schedule unscheduled high-priority tasks, and spot overloaded dates inside active cycle.
incentive: Adds deadline-oriented planning parity while reusing existing task data.

title: Gantt/timeline view visualizes dependencies and critical path
intent: Add a Plane/Jira-class timeline using Fulcrum task start/due dates, dependencies, parent relationships, milestones/modules, and critical path markers.
acceptance: Timeline renders task bars, dependency arrows, module/milestone grouping, and critical path highlight.
Dragging bar start/end updates task dates through service action and records activity.
Blocked dependency violations are visible inline and filterable.
Timeline can open peek/detail and uses same saved view filters.
anti_patterns: Decorative chart disconnected from editable task records.
No dependency arrows or critical path despite timeline label.
Custom hand-rolled SVG when approved library covers core behavior.
interactions: Drag a task end date, observe dependent task risk marker update.
Filter to module, inspect critical path, open blocking task detail.
Switch timeline scale week/month without losing scroll position.
critique_focus: Does timeline reveal delivery risk rather than merely plotting dates?
manual_simulation: Assess whether a module can finish before target date by following highlighted dependency chain and adjusting one task date.
incentive: Turns Fulcrum's dependency graph into a planning surface.

title: Work-item analytics dashboard matches Plane insights plus Fulcrum run metrics
intent: Expand reports with Plane work-item insights and Fulcrum-specific run/doc/memory metrics across project, cycle, module, and workspace scopes.
acceptance: Reports include created vs resolved, state distribution, priority distribution, assignee workload, cycle time, lead time, throughput, WIP, blocked age, and stale items.
Fulcrum adds agent success rate, failed-run count, artifact volume, memory candidates, context size, and automation-trigger metrics.
Insight tables support export CSV and drilldown to saved work views.
Metrics derive from event log/snapshots or documented current substitutes, not UI-only counts.
anti_patterns: Dashboard cards with static counts only.
Charts that cannot drill down to underlying tasks.
Run metrics separated from work management reports.
interactions: Open project analytics, click blocked-age row, land in filtered saved view.
Export work insight CSV for current cycle.
Compare human throughput and agent run success trend.
critique_focus: Do analytics drive planning decisions and agent process improvement?
manual_simulation: Use reports to identify an overloaded assignee, stale blocked tasks, and failing agent workflow before cycle close.
incentive: Makes Fulcrum measurably better than Plane for agentic delivery loops.

title: Mobile work views provide responsive triage, not desktop shrink-wrap
intent: Adapt Plane mobile headers and layout selection patterns so Fulcrum project work is usable on narrow screens for triage, status updates, detail review, and notifications.
acceptance: Mobile workbench has top mobile header with project context, layout menu, filter access, create action, and command access.
Board/list/table/calendar degrade into touch-safe cards or rows with 44px controls.
Task detail opens full-screen with same relationship sections and bottom action bar.
Mobile supports intake triage and notification deep links.
anti_patterns: Horizontal desktop board requiring pinch/scroll for basic triage.
Hiding filters or saved views on mobile.
Mouse-only drag as the only way to move work.
interactions: On mobile viewport, switch layout, open filters, update status, and return to list.
Open intake item from notification and accept into project.
Use command palette on mobile to create task in current project.
critique_focus: Can a user handle urgent triage on phone without feature loss that changes workflow semantics?
manual_simulation: From phone, accept a failed-run follow-up, assign owner, set priority, and add to active cycle.
incentive: Keeps Fulcrum operational outside desktop deep-work sessions.

title: Work item schema adopts Plane semantics plus Fulcrum execution links
intent: Expand Task into WorkItem semantics covering type, state group, labels, assignees, cycle, module, parent/subitems, relations, watchers, estimates, start/due dates, source refs, docs, runs, artifacts, and memory links.
acceptance: Domain model distinguishes work item type, workflow state, and state group.
Relationships cover blocks, blocked_by, relates_to, duplicates, parent, and subitem semantics.
Work item can link docs, repo paths, branches, runs, artifacts, memory entries, and intake sources.
API response DTOs do not expose entities directly and map all relationship counts.
anti_patterns: Adding fields only to UI row type.
Using labels/modules/cycles interchangeably.
Persisting Plane names that describe source provenance rather than Fulcrum responsibility.
interactions: Create task with parent, module, cycle, source doc, and suggested agent workflow.
Add blocker relation and verify both task details update counts.
Link run artifact to task and see it in work item aggregate.
critique_focus: Does model preserve mature PM semantics while making agent execution first-class?
manual_simulation: Model a feature task with subitems, design doc, repo path, active run, output artifact, and memory candidate.
incentive: Prevents UI PRD expansion from exceeding persistence/service truth.

title: Workflow states support groups, transitions, and project schemes
intent: Implement project workflow schemes inspired by Plane states and Jira transitions, where custom states map to canonical groups and allowed transitions are enforced by services.
acceptance: Each project has ordered workflow states mapped to backlog, unstarted, started, completed, cancelled groups.
Transition graph can block illegal moves with actionable error.
Board columns derive from project workflow, not hard-coded status list.
State changes emit event log entries consumed by reports, notifications, and automation.
anti_patterns: Hard-coded task status enum in web as source of truth.
Custom states without canonical group for analytics.
Illegal transition handled only by disabled UI.
interactions: Configure project states, attempt blocked transition, see service error and suggested allowed path.
Drag task across allowed column and inspect activity event.
Filter saved view by state group across projects with different state names.
critique_focus: Can different projects customize workflow without breaking cross-project analytics and saved views?
manual_simulation: Create review-heavy workflow Todo -> In Progress -> In Review -> Done and verify direct Todo -> Done is denied.
incentive: Provides mature PM workflow control and reliable metrics.

title: Bulk toolbar handles selection-wide planning actions
intent: Add Plane/Linear-style bulk selection toolbar for status, priority, assignee, cycle, module, labels, dates, archive, delete, and dispatch actions across board/list/table.
acceptance: Selecting tasks shows toolbar with selected count and safe actions.
Bulk updates validate permissions and transition rules per task and return partial failure details.
Bulk command palette actions mirror toolbar actions.
Selection survives layout switch inside same workbench.
anti_patterns: Bulk actions hidden only inside command palette.
All-or-nothing update with no per-task failure report.
Selection state global across unrelated project navigation.
interactions: Select tasks across status columns and bulk assign cycle.
Bulk change priority from table view and inspect partial failure summary.
Use command palette bulk archive on selected completed tasks.
critique_focus: Can bulk actions handle power-user cleanup without bypassing domain rules?
manual_simulation: After import, select 25 accepted tasks, label them, assign owner, and move valid ones into active cycle while seeing invalid transition failures.
incentive: Reduces high-volume planning friction and makes imports/intake practical.

title: Dependency graph appears in board, detail, and timeline
intent: Make blockers and dependency chains visible across task cards, detail widgets, filters, timeline, and run dispatch context.
acceptance: Task cards show blocked/blocking indicators with hover/peek details.
Detail relation widget supports add/remove blockers, related, duplicate, parent/subitem relationships.
Timeline draws dependency arrows and highlights blocked chain.
Dispatch context preview includes dependency chain and warns on unresolved blockers.
anti_patterns: Dependencies only visible in a separate tree page.
Relation updates that do not emit activity/audit events.
Agent dispatch ignoring blockers.
interactions: Add blocker from detail, see board badge and timeline arrow.
Filter to blocked tasks, open dependency tree, dispatch run only after approving warning.
Mark duplicate intake item and link original task.
critique_focus: Does dependency UX inform both human planning and agent dispatch decisions?
manual_simulation: Before starting a run, inspect whether the task is blocked by an unfinished schema migration and follow the chain to owner.
incentive: Dependency truth is core to safe agent execution and delivery planning.

title: Task activity timeline unifies comments, changes, and run events
intent: Use Plane issue activity patterns to build a Fulcrum timeline containing comments, property changes, relation changes, doc links, run lifecycle, artifact changes, memory proposals, and automation events.
acceptance: Timeline groups events chronologically and distinguishes comments, system changes, run events, and automation.
Comments support mentions, resolve/unresolve where applicable, reactions, and edit/delete permissions.
Property changes show from/to values and actor.
Run events link to run detail, transcript turn, diff, artifact, and trace ids.
anti_patterns: Separate comment tab and audit log with duplicated events.
Timeline only showing human comments.
No stable event ids for trace/audit export.
interactions: Comment with mention, update status, dispatch run, and see all events in order.
Resolve a comment thread and filter timeline to unresolved comments.
Click run event to open run trace drawer.
critique_focus: Does activity timeline become the canonical history for human and agent work?
manual_simulation: Review why a task moved back to In Progress by reading comments, failed run event, artifact update, and QA review in one timeline.
incentive: Turns task detail into durable accountability and audit surface.

title: Project dashboard summarizes work, repo, docs, runs, artifacts, memory, and automations
intent: Expand project overview beyond quick nav into a Plane-like project home plus Fulcrum graph summary showing current work, repo state, docs, runs, artifacts, memory candidates, automations, and reports.
acceptance: Dashboard top shows project name, slug, local path, branch/dirty state, doctor status, active workflow mode, and quick actions.
Work summary includes active cycle, backlog, blocked, due soon, untriaged, and failed-run counts.
Relationship modules show docs, recent runs, artifacts, memory, automations, and reports with drilldowns.
Command palette actions default to current project payload.
anti_patterns: Project page as static metadata and links only.
Hiding repo/run/doc context outside work management.
Metrics computed only client-side from partial rows.
interactions: Open project, immediately see blocked work and failed runs, then drill into filtered view.
Start new task/run/doc from dashboard quick actions.
Navigate to repo dirty state and return to dashboard.
critique_focus: Does dashboard make the full Fulcrum project spine visible?
manual_simulation: Morning project check: inspect branch state, active cycle, blocked agent tasks, recent artifacts, and memory candidates in two minutes.
incentive: Establishes project home as the entry point for supervision, not just CRUD.

title: Notifications route work events to actionable destinations
intent: Adopt Plane notification concepts for watchers/subscribers and extend them to Fulcrum run, artifact, memory, automation, and repo events with deep links.
acceptance: Users can watch projects, cycles, modules, tasks, docs, runs, and saved views.
Notifications deep-link to exact task detail section, run trace, artifact, intake item, or comment.
Notification preferences support in-app, CLI/TUI inbox, desktop/web push when available, and integrations later.
Events dedupe and group noisy run/tool updates.
anti_patterns: Email-only or toast-only notifications.
No subscriber/watch model on tasks.
Deep links opening generic dashboard instead of source object.
interactions: Watch a task, receive notification when agent run fails, open directly to run event in task timeline.
Subscribe to saved view for new blocked P0 work.
Mute noisy automation notifications for one project.
critique_focus: Do notifications help supervise work without becoming noise?
manual_simulation: Leave Fulcrum open, get alerted that a watched task produced memory candidates, jump to task detail, and accept/reject them.
incentive: Closes the loop for asynchronous agent work and human review.

title: Quick create preserves context and supports templates
intent: Implement Plane-like quick create from workbench, calendar, module, cycle, command palette, and intake with contextual defaults, templates, and optional agent workflow suggestion.
acceptance: Quick create pre-fills project, view filters, cycle, module, status, due date, labels, and owner when context provides them.
Templates can add checklist/subtasks, docs, repo path, suggested workflow, and acceptance criteria.
Create can stay inline for title-only or expand to full form.
Created task appears optimistically in current layout and records source context.
anti_patterns: One global create modal that loses where user started.
Required full form for every task.
Templates detached from workflow/run dispatch.
interactions: In calendar, quick-create on date with current cycle prefilled.
From module page, create task with module and doc template.
Use command palette to create run-ready task from template.
critique_focus: Does quick create minimize interruption while capturing enough context for agent-ready work?
manual_simulation: During planning, add ten tasks into active cycle with due dates and templates without leaving calendar/list context.
incentive: Fast capture is required for Plane-level planning fluidity.

title: Work events publish to reports, notifications, automation, audit, and agent context
intent: Define producer/consumer map for all work-management changes so task edits drive metrics, notifications, automation, audit trails, and agent dispatch context.
acceptance: Every create/update/delete/relation/comment/run-link/action emits typed event with actor, causation id, project id, task id, and metadata.
Consumers include activity timeline, analytics snapshots, notifications, automation, audit export, search indexing, and context preview invalidation.
Event schema covers status, assignment, priority, label, cycle, module, date, dependency, comment, doc link, run, artifact, memory, and intake changes.
Tests prove at least three consumers react to the same event without interface layers owning business logic.
anti_patterns: Reports polling current task rows only.
Automation triggered directly from web action handlers.
Audit events missing causation ids or source refs.
interactions: Move task to blocked and observe activity, notification, saved-view count, and automation candidate update.
Dispatch run from task and see context preview invalidated and run event emitted.
Export task trace as JSON.
critique_focus: Is this an integration spine, or just another log table?
manual_simulation: Trace one task from intake acceptance through status changes, run dispatch, artifact creation, and closure using event ids.
incentive: Prevents PRD expansion from creating disconnected features with no workflow truth.

title: CLI and TUI expose same workbench semantics as web
intent: Ensure Plane-inspired work features do not become web-only by mapping saved views, filters, task detail, cycles, modules, intake, and dispatch flows into CLI/TUI commands and screens.
acceptance: CLI can list saved views, apply filters, open task detail aggregate, update properties, manage cycles/modules, and dispatch run.
TUI can navigate project -> saved view -> workbench -> task detail -> run preview/dispatch.
CLI/TUI use shared application services or tRPC caller, never duplicate business logic.
Parity tests cover web/CLI/TUI for one saved view and one dispatch-from-task flow.
anti_patterns: Web-only features with CLI separate task model.
TUI hard-coded screens that ignore saved views.
CLI commands requiring IDs for every action when current project/view context exists.
interactions: Run CLI command to list blocked saved view and dispatch run for a task.
Use TUI to change status, inspect dependencies, and open run preview.
Compare counts between web saved view and CLI saved view output.
critique_focus: Do text surfaces preserve semantics or only provide partial convenience?
manual_simulation: In terminal, select active project saved view, inspect blocked task detail, update priority, and start a run without opening browser.
incentive: Fulcrum's identity is multi-surface local-first supervision.

title: Imports and sync feed intake with source fidelity
intent: Use Plane parity gaps to define imports from GitHub/GitLab/Jira/Linear/Asana and repo scans as intake sources, preserving external ids and sync status before accepted tasks enter the board.
acceptance: Import preview shows external source, id, title, state, labels, assignee, comments summary, and conflict/duplicate status.
Imported items land in intake unless user explicitly imports as tasks.
Accepted task keeps source ref and can later sync comments/status when integration supports it.
Duplicate detection can link imported item to existing task without creating a new task.
anti_patterns: Blind import directly into board.
Dropping external ids after conversion.
One-off importer bypassing intake/event/audit model.
interactions: Import GitHub issues preview, accept three, decline duplicates, and inspect source refs.
Re-run import and see unchanged/updated/new grouping.
Open task detail and jump to external source.
critique_focus: Does import create trustworthy work records instead of one-time data dump?
manual_simulation: Bring 50 GitHub issues into Fulcrum, triage only actionable ones, and preserve links for future sync.
incentive: Makes migration from existing trackers viable while protecting board quality.

title: Work actions honor role, project, and view access
intent: Carry Plane's permission-aware work controls into Fulcrum so project membership, view access, and command visibility are enforced server-side and reflected in UI.
acceptance: Task, cycle, module, view, intake, and command actions declare required permission.
Server rejects unauthorized actions with domain error mapped to HTTP/tRPC.
UI hides or disables unavailable actions and explains permission when visible.
Saved views support private, project, workspace access semantics.
anti_patterns: Client-only permission gating.
Every user can execute command palette actions.
Private saved views implemented by naming convention.
interactions: Open read-only project and verify edit commands absent.
Try forbidden bulk delete via API and receive mapped permission error.
Share view with project and verify other project member can open it.
critique_focus: Does permission model stay central as Power-K and bulk actions expand?
manual_simulation: As a viewer, browse task detail and saved views, then attempt status change from command palette and confirm blocked behavior.
incentive: Prevents high-power work controls from becoming data-loss hazards.

title: Archive and restore work without losing history
intent: Implement Plane-style archive behavior for tasks, cycles, modules, views, and intake items so users can declutter while preserving activity, metrics, and restore paths.
acceptance: Archive removes items from default active views but keeps archived section and searchable history.
Restore revalidates current workflow/project existence and returns item to appropriate state/view.
Archived items keep activity, comments, relations, run/artifact links, and source refs.
Reports can include or exclude archived items explicitly.
anti_patterns: Hard delete as normal declutter action.
Archived tasks silently disappearing from audit and linked docs.
Restore that loses cycle/module relation.
interactions: Archive completed stale task, find it in archives, restore it, inspect history retained.
Archive a closed cycle and filter reports excluding it.
Try to archive task with active run and receive warning.
critique_focus: Does archive serve PM hygiene without breaking auditability?
manual_simulation: Clean a project board after release while preserving artifacts and run history for postmortem.
incentive: Keeps long-lived local workspaces usable and auditable.

title: Workspace sidebar exposes projects, views, cycles, modules, and recents
intent: Use Plane's workspace/project sidebar density to make Fulcrum navigation expose project hierarchy, favorite views, active cycles, modules, recents, inbox, notifications, and command entry.
acceptance: Sidebar includes workspace/project switcher, project list, favorites, saved views, active cycles, inbox, notifications, and recent work.
Collapsed mode preserves icons/tooltips and keyboard navigation.
Sidebar selection reflects current route and current project context for command palette.
Recents update from actual visits, not static list.
anti_patterns: Top nav only with no persistent PM structure.
Sidebar links not scoped to current workspace/project.
Recents based on browser history only.
interactions: Favorite a saved view and open it from sidebar.
Collapse sidebar, use keyboard to jump to active cycle.
Switch project and verify command payload changes.
critique_focus: Does navigation make complex work structures discoverable without overwhelming foundation app surfaces?
manual_simulation: Move between three projects, active cycle, blocked saved view, and inbox without using browser back or search.
incentive: Dense PM navigation is required once modules/views/intake exist.

title: Users control columns and card properties per view
intent: Copy Plane display property controls so users decide which fields show on cards, list rows, spreadsheets, calendar chips, and detail peeks.
acceptance: Saved view stores display properties per layout and project/workspace scope.
Card and row properties can include state, priority, assignee, labels, cycle, module, dates, blockers, run state, docs, artifacts, and estimates.
Spreadsheet columns are reorderable, sortable where supported, and exportable.
Display property changes are previewed before saving view.
anti_patterns: One fixed card design for every use case.
Spreadsheet columns hard-coded in component.
Display toggles not persisted.
interactions: Hide assignee and show run state on board cards, save view.
Add blockers and docs count to spreadsheet columns, sort by priority.
Switch to peek and confirm selected properties carry over.
critique_focus: Does customization help different Fulcrum workflows without fragmenting underlying data?
manual_simulation: Create an 'agent supervision' view showing run state, last artifact, blockers, and context age instead of sprint-only fields.
incentive: Lets Fulcrum exceed Plane by surfacing agent-specific work properties.

title: Work automations operate on task events and command actions
intent: Tie Plane-style workflow automation to Fulcrum's task events so status changes, labels, cycles, run results, docs, and memory candidates can trigger service-owned actions.
acceptance: Automation rule builder supports trigger, condition, action summary and validation.
Triggers include task created, state changed, priority changed, due date changed, run failed/succeeded, artifact created, memory candidate emitted, and intake accepted.
Actions include assign, label, move state, add comment, create follow-up, notify, dispatch run preview, and link doc template.
Automation executions appear in task activity and audit trace.
anti_patterns: Automation logic in UI components.
Rules that directly start destructive actions without preview/permission control.
No execution history for rules.
interactions: Create rule: when run fails twice, label blocked and notify owner.
Create rule: when task enters Done, request QA review run preview.
Inspect automation event in task timeline.
critique_focus: Can automations reduce supervision toil while respecting permissions and traceability?
manual_simulation: Configure failed-agent-run escalation and watch a task automatically move to blocked with a comment and notification.
incentive: Makes Fulcrum operationally useful for repeated agent supervision loops.
